title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench (study_id = rX4f7-1), a paired comparison of a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline on 1,200 intent→config episodes (planned episodes = 2,400; completed episodes = 2,398; complete paired observations = 1,199). Using the requested model gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and Mininet‑style emulation, we applied a preregistered binary episode success rule (validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback). Observed pooled outcomes were: baseline successes = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149), guarded successes = 1,199/1,199 (1.0000000000), paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025020851. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.0058381985] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). Provider audit shows model_calls_used = 1,203 and repair calls invoked = 3. The preregistered confirmatory topology‑cluster breakdown (H3) was not executed as a separate confirmatory contrast; the archived analysis contains only the pooled paired confirmatory results (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json). Under these task, validator, and emulation choices we observed no statistically significant advantage for the verifier‑assisted pipeline; archived artifacts and diagnostics indicate the null result reflects near‑ceiling baseline performance and infrequent repair invocation rather than proof that verifiers are never useful.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent expressed in natural language into executable device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Prior surveys and system work emphasize that operational reliability depends on the orchestration stack (model + verifier + provenance + sandboxed execution) rather than on the LLM alone and that generate–validate–repair architectures are a canonical mitigation strategy [http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12708/229494, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13389].

We designed NetOpsTraceBench to answer a focused question: can a reproducible, workflow‑centered, paired benchmark of intent→config episodes produce an objective paired binary success metric that distinguishes a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline from a one‑shot generation baseline? The study was preregistered (rX4f7-1) and frozen prior to model access. Key contributions: (1) a preregistered paired design and full archived execution artifacts; (2) a pooled confirmatory analysis on 1,199 complete pairs run with the requested model gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator; (3) transparent accounting and interpretation showing repair was rarely required (repair calls = 3) and the observed pooled difference was small and not statistically significant.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers position LLMs as components within broader AIOps/NetOps workflows and call for workflow‑centered evaluation that records generator traces, verifier interactions, and emulated execution-side effects [https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13389, http://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09369, https://doi.org/10.3390/app16010085]. Verifier‑assisted generator loops appear across domains (NL→formal spec, topology compilation, misconfiguration detection) and often show localized gains when verifier rules capture the domain constraints precisely; however, these demonstrations typically evaluate on constructed or narrow datasets and thus motivate reproducible, preregistered paired comparisons [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6947162, https://doi.org/10.3390/info17030297].

Empirical studies catalog LLM failure modes relevant to NetOps—hallucination, unit/semantic errors, overconfidence, provenance loss, prompt‑injection risks—which motivate guarded architectures yet also underscore that measured benefit depends on task difficulty and verifier strictness [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7222278, https://doi.org/10.20935/acadai8260]. NetOpsTraceBench implements these workflow recommendations and records deterministic validator traces and emulator outcomes to make such dependencies observable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design: The study preregistration (rX4f7-1; preregistration SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) froze the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), inclusion/exclusion rules, seeds, stopping rules, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The prespecified confirmatory hypothesis H1 concerned a paired difference in binary episode success; H3 in the preregistration specified a topology‑cluster breakdown (edge vs core) as a confirmatory subgroup contrast.

Important disclosure about H3 (topology clusters): The preregistration included H3; the archived confirmatory analysis executed and archived only the pooled paired test. The preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory breakdown (H3) was not executed as a separate confirmatory inference in the archived analysis artifacts. The authoritative archived confirmatory artifacts are analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, and execution/execution_manifest.json, which contain the pooled counts and inference reported here. Per‑cluster analyses therefore remain outside the preregistered confirmatory set and should be treated as future exploratory work unless explicitly archived as additional confirmatory artifacts.

Task corpus, conditions, and deterministic components: The benchmark used 1,200 deterministically generated tasks (task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, generator_version = 5.0) split conceptually into two simulated topology clusters (edge/core) in the preregistration; tasks include structured payloads (initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, workflow_policies) and a declared difficulty label. Inclusion/exclusion rules (contamination thresholds T_contam = 0.85 and optional embedding checks) and missingness rules were enforced deterministically. The execution adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Per preregistration, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and generation_semantics used a shared_initial_candidate so baseline and guarded episodes within each pair used the same initial LLM candidate to isolate verifier and repair effects. Model configuration recorded requested_model = gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens = 1500 (see execution/model_configuration.json).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: The run completed 2,398 of 2,400 planned episodes and produced 1,199 complete paired observations (complete_pairs = 1,199). Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1) and stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 1,200 and repair = 3, consistent with archived provider traces (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Primary pooled confirmatory outcomes (archived artifacts): The pooled paired 2×2 contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 1,196, n10 = 3, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts: baseline successes = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076 and guarded successes = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446. Exact McNemar two‑sided test on the discordant counts yields p = 0.25 (archived in analysis/results.json). The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) is [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957], archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/results.json.

Missingness and repairs: The missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) reports failed_baseline_episodes = 1, failed_guarded_episodes = 1, and both_missing_pairs = 1; no contamination exclusions were triggered (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty). Repair invocation was observed in exactly three episodes (stage_counts repair = 3), and representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) show that for the vast majority of episodes validation_after.valid == true and repair_applied == false, explaining the low discordant count.

Topline interpretation anchored in artifacts: The pooled confirmatory analysis therefore finds no statistically significant improvement for the guarded pipeline under the archived corpus and validator configuration (p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). The archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/scoring/*.json) support two operationally relevant facts: (1) baseline one‑shot generation already achieved near‑ceiling success on the supplied synthetic/consented corpus (≈99.75%), and (2) the guarded pipeline's repair loop was rarely invoked (3 repairs), limiting measurable headroom for pooled confirmatory gains.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation: The pooled null result should be interpreted considering preregistered power planning and observed data characteristics. The preregistered power target sought a 5 percentage‑point MDE under assumed baseline ≈0.70; the observed baseline ≈0.9975 substantially reduces power to detect small absolute improvements. The small number of discordant pairs (3 of 1,199) yields an exact McNemar p = 0.25 and a bootstrap CI whose lower bound reaches 0.0, quantitatively documenting limited resolution for small effects.

Shared‑candidate pairing and repair frequency: The design used a shared_initial_candidate per pair (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") so both conditions evaluated the same initial LLM output; this choice isolates verifier/repair effects but also means that if the initial candidate already satisfies deterministic validator constraints (as happened in most episodes), the guarded pipeline will rarely exercise repair. This mechanistic fact is anchored in provider audit and stage_counts (shared_initial_generation = 1,200; repair = 3) and explains why repair invocation was infrequent. Practitioners and future benchmarks should consider experimental variations that (a) allow independent generation across conditions to measure model variance effects, (b) increase task ambiguity/adversariality to create repair demand, or (c) vary verifier strictness to probe sensitivity.

H3 and per‑cluster inference: The preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory breakdown (H3) was not executed as a separate confirmatory contrast in the archived analysis; the authoritative archived confirmatory artifacts contain only the pooled paired analysis. Because per‑cluster confirmatory contrasts were not archived, the manuscript does not report per‑cluster inferential outcomes—and any per‑cluster summaries would be exploratory unless re‑archived under a preregistered confirmatory plan. This explicit statement aligns the reported analyses with the archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/results.json; execution/execution_manifest.json).

Threats to validity and externality: Internal validity is supported by deterministic seeds, automated exclusion rules, and archived logs; construct validity depends on whether the binary success rule maps to operationally meaningful correctness across heterogeneous production settings. External validity is limited by a single requested model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic/consented task corpus that yielded near‑ceiling baseline performance, and Mininet‑style emulation that may not capture vendor idiosyncrasies and routing convergence dynamics. Different verifier strictness or more adversarial tasks could materially change repair invocation and discordant counts.
sections.conclusion: NetOpsTraceBench produced a fully archived, preregistered paired comparison of one‑shot vs verifier‑assisted NL→configuration pipelines. Under the supplied synthetic/consented corpus, deterministic validator settings, and requested model gpt-5-mini, the pooled confirmatory analysis on 1,199 pairs shows a small absolute improvement favoring the guarded pipeline (0.25 percentage points) that is not statistically significant (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% bootstrap CI includes zero). Archived provider audits (model_calls_used = 1,203; repair calls = 3) and validator traces demonstrate that initial candidates were accepted most often, limiting measurable guard value on this corpus. The preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory contrast (H3) was not executed as a separate confirmatory test in the archived analysis; the archived confirmatory artifacts contain only pooled results (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json). Future work should target more challenging and adversarial tasks, vary verifier strictness, and test multiple model families to identify conditions under which verifier scaffolding yields operationally meaningful improvements. All run artifacts (raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, task manifests, analysis code, and seeds) are archived to permit exact reproduction and planned exploratory follow‑ups.

limitations: Single model family tested (requested_model = gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.

Task corpus skew: deterministic synthetic/consented tasks produced near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture vendor idiosyncrasies, routing convergence phenomena, or transient telemetry seen in live deployments.

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test appropriate for paired binary outcomes. This deviation and its rationale are recorded in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Per‑cluster confirmatory inference absent: the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory contrast (H3) was not executed as a separate archived confirmatory analysis; per‑cluster inference is therefore not supported by the archived confirmatory artifacts and remains an avenue for exploratory or future preregistered work.
